answer: A new agent may transact only after seasoning a unique timber certificate for 14 days, and during that wait it must publish an on-ledger pulse every eight hours that hashes a fresh paid inference receipt. Standing is a dune: each peer-checked pulse adds a thin layer, but a missed pulse erodes two layers, so a burst of clones quickly sinks to zero. Anyone can verify the receipt hash and the certificate serial on-ledger. If two identities reuse the same receipt or serial, both certificates are burned, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times one honest bond.
